newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 sets week's third closing record.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 sets week's third closing record.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index powered to its third record close of the week on Friday as gilts extended Thursday's sharp gains and Wall Street advanced.

Ending above 4,200 for the first time ever, the index closed 10.2 points higher at 4,207.7, in a day dominated for many trading desks by the sale of 135 million Guinness shares by LVMH of France -- which pushed trading volume to over 1 billion shares.
The FTSE 250 index of midcap stocks also set a record, up 17.5 points at 4,583.4, surpassing its peak of 4568.6 set as long ago as April 1996.

Though UK shares may consolidate short-term, dealers said the market may not loose its fizz until the end of the month when concerns about U.S. rates may return to the fore ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy-making session on February 4.

They said this week's decision to leave rates unchanged, coupled with benign inflation numbers, should continue to underpin the market as investment funds running high cash positions were caught flat-footed by the FTSE's recent run.
"The economic indicators continue to look fairly benign and it is now a question of whether the institutions are confident to pursue the market at its current levels," said one.
"At the moment the feeling is we do not need to worry about rising rates but we may get a bit more nervous ahead of the FOMC meeting."
The Dow was up some 26 points as London closed and Treasury bonds recovered from initial weakness as a report in the Washington Post said the Fed appeared unlikely to raise rates anytime soon.

The report helped to counter today's stronger-than-expected industrial production and capacity utilisation figures that could otherwise have revived fears that economic expansion could prompt a rate rise.
U.S. markets also took comfort from news that the U.S. trade gap in November had undercut forecasts.
Gilts ended higher but off their day's best with the long gilt future up 1/4 at 111, extending Tursday's rise of just under a full point.
Earlier, amid expiry of index options, the FTSE 100 leapt to an intraday high of 4,218.4, breaching 4,200 for the first time.

"We look to be in an arena of low inflation and low interest rates," said another dealer. "Even though there's political uncertainty round the corner, the market will continue to reflect Wall Street, which is a raging bull at the moment."
Meanwhile the death of a Conservative member of parliament yesterday pushed Prime Minister John Major's government into a minority and fuelled speculation about an early election.
"It now seems inevitable that an election will be called early and the Chancellor will no doubt try to hold interest rates down if he can," said one dealer.

LVMH's surprise sale of a third of its stake in Guinness provided one of the day's big talking points, sending Guinness shares down 22p at one stage though they rallied by the close to be down just 4p at 432. Guinness said its joint distribution deals with LVMH were unaffected by the sale.
Allied Domecq was another victim of the sale, down 6p at 411-1/2 as some investors sold their Allied shares to make way for extra Guinness stock.

Demerging conglomerate Hanson was also heavily traded, closing up 3-1/2p at 92-1/2 in volume of 46.8 million, amid U.S. buying following positive comment from the company's broker ABN AMRO Hoare Govett earlier this week.
Building materials group Redland was another major gainer, up 9-1/2p at 343-1/2 as a number of analysts became more positive about the stock following a meeting with company executives.

In the retail sector Storehouse rose 16-1/2p to 274 and Blacks Leisure rose 15-1/2p to 400-1/2 after well-received trading statements. In a still-bouyant bank sector Bank of Scotland rose 4p to 333-1/2 as Goldman Sachs analysts raised earnings estimates.
British Borneo rose 28-1/2p to 11.07-1/2 stg after positive comment from analysts at Hoare Govett.

Major decliners in the FTSE 100 included P&O, down 19p at 623 after UBS cut the stock to "hold," while Imperial Chemical Industries also fell victim to UBS comment, down 3-1/2p at 738-1/2 as the brokerage cut profit estimates.
-- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
